_note: Chains and the short token list of /swap/. Everything here was read from LI.FI's own service on 2026-11-23 (/v1/chains for the networks and their diamond contract, /v1/tokens for the tokens), never from memory. Kept: EVM mainnets whose native coin has 18 decimals, that publish a contract, an https node and an https explorer, and for which a real quote came back — the transaction of that quote was addressed to exactly the contract pinned here, on 40 of 40 networks and 14 different routing tools. Each chain's `contract` is what assets/swap/swap.js demands: a transaction addressed anywhere else is refused, so if LI.FI ever moves it the swap stops instead of going somewhere unknown. Only tokens LI.FI marks as verified are listed, one per symbol; a reader can reach any other token by typing its symbol or address, which the page looks up live. tests/test_swap.py checks every address's EIP-55 checksum. Added on the same day from the same service: LI.FI's six networks that are not EVM (Bitcoin, Tron, Solana, Sui, Stellar, Zcash), each marked to_only because a swap may end there but not start there — starting there needs a wallet of that network's own kind, and LI.FI itself refuses it until a fee wallet for that network is registered in the portal. Also added: the large coins that were missing from the EVM lists, each kept only where LI.FI's own coinKey matches the symbol, which is what keeps the look-alikes out (Tron's list carries 'US DT', 'U S D T' and 'UDST' beside the real USDT). Widened once more the same day: a coin was added only where two independent sources agree on it — LI.FI's /v1/tokens offers it (with a picture and a live price) and Trust Wallet's reviewed-assets repository lists the very same contract as active, with the same decimals. Where two contracts on one network wear one symbol, the one on Trust Wallet's own short list was taken, or neither. Checked again against the live service on 2026-11-24: all 593 contracts were read back from LI.FI and every one agreed on its decimals; a dozen symbols that Trust Wallet spells differently were set to the spelling LI.FI uses, and the superseded USDD contracts, which sat beside the current ones under a name one letter apart, were dropped. On 2026-11-24 fee wallets for Tron and Solana were registered in the LI.FI portal and both began to answer as the start of a swap, so they are no longer to_only. Tron carries LI.FI's own contract there (diamondAddress from /v1/chains), which every Tron transaction is held to; Solana has no such single address. Bitcoin stays to_only: /v1/quote and /v1/advanced/stepTransaction do not answer for it.
